textual.observation: The speaker describes a referral-based team structure where viewers can place recruits on a left or right side, with team building tied to a promised weekly bonus.

evidence.quote: you can pick a link. That will let someone sign up to your left or right side
The reason why you want that bonus is because you're going to get paid weekly.

textual.context: Promotional first-person framing; the speaker is inviting viewers to join his team rather than reporting or warning about the program.
textual.potential_relevance: The records link using a referral link and placing recruits into team positions with a promised weekly payment, creating a recruitment-and-compensation relationship for later context assessment.
textual.limitations: The records do not establish whether payments occurred, whether the program operated as described, or whether the linked destination produced the stated outcome.

textual.observation: The speaker presents Bitcoin as a rising long-term investment and connects that opportunity to joining his team to grow Bitcoin holdings.

evidence.quote: this it's a good longterm investment. I'm telling you the five-year forecast is up to 15008
I want to invite you guys to join my team and spread the word. It's a great opportunity, especially if you're trying to grow your Bitcoin.

textual.context: The investment and growth statements are presented affirmatively by the speaker in a promotional context.
textual.potential_relevance: A stated Bitcoin growth and price-forecast claim is paired with a request to join the speaker's team, linking a promised financial outcome to a recruitment action.
textual.limitations: The records do not provide an independent basis for the forecast, clarify the quoted figure, or establish any realized return.

visual.observation: A membership dashboard displays team counts and direct referrals alongside bonus balances, trading balances, and total funds in a pool; another page displays a registration link and specific placement registration links.
visual.context: The visible pages are an account dashboard and referral-link section. It is unclear from the sampled frames whether viewers are being actively recruited or how the referral arrangement operates beyond the displayed links and account categories.
visual.potential_relevance: The visible registration links are connected to referral and team-member tracking, while the dashboard shows bonuses and fund balances, creating an observable relationship between a requested registration action and potential referral-related financial returns.
visual.limitations: These frames do not establish whether any person registered, paid, transferred assets, received bonuses, or obtained the displayed balances, and they do not establish the legitimacy or terms of the program.

visual.observation: A banner on a cryptocurrency-related page states “TRADE 24/7, SAME DAY WITHDRAWALS, LIVE CHAT SUPPORT” and includes a “TRADE NOW” call to action.
visual.context: This appears as a promotional banner displayed on a Bitcoin forecasting page; the sampled frame does not show additional terms or qualifications for the withdrawal statement.
visual.potential_relevance: The banner links a trading action to a stated same-day withdrawal outcome, which is a return-related claim connected to an instructed action.
visual.limitations: The frames do not establish who operates the service, whether same-day withdrawals are available, what conditions apply, or whether anyone traded or withdrew funds.

visual.observation: A page headed “The official wallet app by Bitcoin.com” presents an option to download and start using a wallet, while another visible section offers Bitcoin purchases using a credit or debit card and includes a wallet-address field.
visual.context: The pages visibly present themselves as Bitcoin.com wallet and purchase interfaces. The supplied frames do not show a completed purchase or download.
visual.potential_relevance: A claimed official identity is directly connected to downloading a wallet and purchasing cryptocurrency through a payment-card and wallet-address interface, making the claimed affiliation and destination relevant for review.
visual.limitations: The frames cannot verify the claimed affiliation, website ownership, wallet destination, payment processing, transaction completion, or any resulting outcome.

visual_context_notes.observation: The referral section visibly labels its links as “REGISTRATION LINK” and “SPECIFIC PLACEMENT REGISTRATION LINKS.”
The dashboard labels the account as “Paid Member” and displays “Direct Referrals,” “Left Team,” “Right Team,” bonus categories, and pool-fund balances.
The cryptocurrency page shows forecast and trading-related content adjacent to the banner containing the “TRADE NOW” call to action.
The Bitcoin.com pages visibly use the wording “The official wallet app by Bitcoin.com” and show a cryptocurrency purchase interface with a wallet-address field.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is scam content because it promotes joining the speaker's team through registration links, team-building positions, and weekly bonus payments tied to specified trading-pool balances. It also claims Bitcoin is a good long-term investment and invites participation to grow Bitcoin, providing a financial-benefit rationale for the requested action. The material does not establish that anyone paid, received a bonus, or realized a return, and the separate Bitcoin.com pages and trading banner are not shown to be connected to the team program.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The speaker links weekly payment to building a two-sided team, describes trading-pool and participant qualifications for the binary bonus, and invites viewers to join through a team URL.
